title: 所: the concept of place
summary: ところ is a place, and then a point in a thing or a point in time: ところだ means about to, in the middle of, or just done.

blocks.text: **ところ** (所) begins as a physical **place**: 私のところ, "my place". Japanese stretches the idea much further than English does.
A place in a thing: an aspect
A person or object has "places" too: the parts or points of it. Asking どこが好き? about a person means "which point do you like?".

blocks.jp: さくらのやさしいところが好きだ。
分からないところがあった。
blocks.en: There were parts I did not understand.

blocks.text: A place in time: ところだ
Put a clause before ところ and you point at a **moment**. The sentence ends in だ, so it is an "A is B" sentence: "the present moment is the place of ...". The tense of the clause chooses the point.

blocks.jp: 今から昼ご飯を食べるところだ。
blocks.en: I am just about to eat lunch.

blocks.jp: 今、昼ご飯を食べているところだ。
blocks.en: I am in the middle of eating lunch right now.

blocks.jp: 昼ご飯を食べたところだ。

blocks.text: Compare **ばかり** (lesson 27): 食べたばかり is close to 食べたところ. But ばかり can follow a plain noun (パンばかり) and ところ cannot, because "a place of bread" says nothing about amount.
In casual speech だ may vanish and ところ shortens to **とこ**: 今、着いたとこ. And context decides between meanings: いいところに来たね is probably "you came at a good moment".

items: **ところ** = place, a part of something, or a moment.
**Dictionary form + ところだ**: about to.
**〜ているところだ**: in the middle of.

questions.prompt: 昼ご飯を食べるところだ。
options: I am about to eat lunch

questions.prompt: 昼ご飯を食べているところだ。
options: I am in the middle of eating lunch
I am about to eat lunch

questions.prompt: 昼ご飯を食べたところだ。
options: I am about to eat lunch

questions.instruction: What does ところ mean in 彼のいいところ?
questions.note: A place in a person means an aspect.

questions.instruction: Why can ばかり say "only bread" (パンばかり) but ところ cannot?
options: ところ means a place or point in time, not an amount
questions.note: "A place of bread" does not make sense.

questions.instruction: What does this casual sentence mean?
options: I have just arrived in Nagoya
I will arrive in Nagoya soon

questions.instruction: What is the most likely meaning?
options: You came at a good moment
You came to a good city

questions.prompt: I am just about to leave the house.

questions.prompt: ところ can only mean a physical place.
questions.note: It also means aspects and moments.
